monuments.name: Tokyo Tower (東京タワー)
monuments.architect: 333m International Orange & White Seismic Steel Lattice Tower (Tachū Naitō & Nikken Sekkei, 1958)
monuments.architecturalStyle: 333m International Orange & White Seismic Steel Lattice Tower (Tachū Naitō & Nikken Sekkei, 1958)
monuments.fact: Designed by seismic structural pioneer Dr. Tachū Naitō and completed in December 1958 at 333 meters—partially forged from recycled steel—standing as the radiant symbol of post-war Tokyo’s rebirth above Shiba Park.

monuments.name: Tokyo Skytree (東京スカイツリー)
monuments.localName: Tokyo Skytree (東京スカイツリー)
monuments.architect: 634m Neo-Futurist Steel Lattice & Five-Story Pagoda Shinbashira Core Damper (Nikken Sekkei, 2012)
monuments.architecturalStyle: 634m Neo-Futurist Steel Lattice & Five-Story Pagoda Shinbashira Core Damper (Nikken Sekkei, 2012)
monuments.fact: Soaring 634 meters (a play on "Mu-sa-shi", the historic province of Tokyo), the world’s tallest broadcasting tower morphs from an equilateral triangle at its base into a circle at 350m, stabilized inside by a central concrete shinbashira inspired by ancient Japanese five-story pagodas.

monuments.name: Sensō-ji Temple, Five-Story Pagoda & Kaminarimon (浅草寺)
monuments.localName: Sensō-ji Temple, Five-Story Pagoda & Kaminarimon (浅草寺)
monuments.architect: Vermilion Buddhist Hondō Hall, Five-Story Gojū-no-tō Pagoda & Kaminarimon Thunder Gate
monuments.architecturalStyle: Vermilion Buddhist Hondō Hall, Five-Story Gojū-no-tō Pagoda & Kaminarimon Thunder Gate
monuments.fact: Founded in 645 AD to enshrine a golden statue of Kannon pulled from the Sumida River; in December 1927, Asia’s very first subway line (the Ginza Line) opened between Asakusa and Ueno to carry worshippers to Sensō-ji’s vermilion Kaminarimon gate and five-story pagoda.

monuments.name: Tokyo Station Marunouchi Building (東京駅丸の内駅舎)
monuments.localName: Tokyo Station Marunouchi Building (東京駅丸の内駅舎)
monuments.architect: 335m Tatsuno-Style Red Brick, White Granite Bands & Twin Octagonal Copper Domes (Kingo Tatsuno, 1914)
monuments.architecturalStyle: 335m Tatsuno-Style Red Brick, White Granite Bands & Twin Octagonal Copper Domes (Kingo Tatsuno, 1914)
monuments.fact: Designed by Kingo Tatsuno and inaugurated on December 20, 1914 facing the Imperial Palace; its 335-meter red-brick facade survived the 1923 Great Kantō Earthquake and had its original three-story octagonal domes faithfully restored in 2012.

monuments.localName: Meiji Jingu Grand Torii & Sanctuary (明治神宮)
monuments.architect: 12m Taiwanese Hinoki Cypress Myōjin Torii & Copper-Roofed Nagare-zukuri Shrine Complex (Chūta Itō, 1920)
monuments.architecturalStyle: 12m Taiwanese Hinoki Cypress Myōjin Torii & Copper-Roofed Nagare-zukuri Shrine Complex (Chūta Itō, 1920)
monuments.fact: Dedicated in November 1920 to Emperor Meiji and Empress Shōken amidst a sacred forest of 100,000 trees donated from across Japan, entered through towering unpainted 1,500-year-old cypress Torii gates next to Harajuku Station.

monuments.name: Tokyo Imperial Palace: Nijūbashi & Fujimi-yagura (皇居二重橋)
monuments.localName: Tokyo Imperial Palace: Nijūbashi & Fujimi-yagura (皇居二重橋)
monuments.architect: Edo Castle Battered Stone Moat Walls, Three-Tiered White Fujimi-yagura Turret & Double-Arch Nijūbashi Bridge
monuments.architecturalStyle: Edo Castle Battered Stone Moat Walls, Three-Tiered White Fujimi-yagura Turret & Double-Arch Nijūbashi Bridge
monuments.fact: Former fortress of the Tokugawa Shogunate (Edo Castle) and residence of the Emperor since the 1868 Meiji Restoration, where the graceful Meiji double-arch Eyeglass Bridge (Nijūbashi) reflects in the moat below the 1659 Fujimi-yagura watchtower.

monuments.architecturalStyle: 204m Elliptical White Diagrid Exoskeleton & Three Curved Indigo Glass Blades (Tange Associates, 2008)
monuments.fact: Designed by Tange Associates in the Nishi-Shinjuku skyscraper district to house three design and technology academies, its sculpted 50-story white diagrid cocoon symbolizes nurturing creative students before they take flight.

monuments.name: Rainbow Bridge (レインボーブリッジ)
monuments.localName: Rainbow Bridge (レインボーブリッジ)
monuments.architect: 798m Double-Deck White Suspension Bridge & Solar-Lit Catenary Cables (1993)
monuments.architecturalStyle: 798m Double-Deck White Suspension Bridge & Solar-Lit Catenary Cables (1993)
monuments.fact: Spanning northern Tokyo Bay between Shibaura Pier and the waterfront islands of Odaiba, its 126-meter white steel H-pylons carry two decks of highway, promenade, and automated transit illuminated at night in rainbow solar LEDs.
